verses.53:4: {deus} escutai a minha oração: * {auribus} palavras da minha boca.
verses.53:5: Porque {alieni} se {insurrexerunt} contra mim, e {fortes} buscaram {animam}: * e não puseram {deum} {conspectum}.
verses.53:6: Pois eis que Deus {adjuvat}: * e o Senhor é o {susceptor} {animae}.

decisions.why: Two verses in a row open on the bare vocative 'Deus,'. The glossary's rule (no 'ó' unless the Latin has 'o') is written for Dóminus; a bare 'Deus,' at the head of a Portuguese sentence is more abrupt than 'Senhor,'. Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and the Diurnal Monástico 1962 all write 'ó Deus' here. Whatever is chosen will serve every 'Deus,' vocative in the psalter, the opening versicle of the Hours included.

options.label: Deus,
options.note: Draft. The Latin's word and nothing else; the same rule as for 'Senhor,'. The anaphora Deus … / Deus … is heard as it stands in the Latin column.

options.label: Ó Deus,
options.note: Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and DM1962 (all after the verb: 'Salva-me, ó Deus'). More native as an invocation and one syllable nearer the Latin's De-us; adds an interjection the Latin does not have.

decisions.latin: in nómine tuo … in virtúte tua … in veritáte tua
decisions.why: The Latin 'in' stands for the Greek ἐν (ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου), which is both 'in' and 'by means of'. Matos Soares 1932 ('por teu nome … com o teu poder'), pt-PT and Douay-Rheims ('by thy name … in thy strength') settle for the instrument, and not even consistently; the Latin keeps one preposition for both, and again in 53:7 (in veritáte tua), where Matos Soares himself keeps 'na tua verdade'.

options.label: no vosso nome … no vosso poder
options.note: Draft. One preposition three times (53:3 twice, 53:7), as in the Latin, and as open as the Latin between 'in' and 'by'. 'Em nome de' is also heard as 'on the authority of', which the Latin phrase can be heard as too.

options.label: em vosso nome … no vosso poder
options.note: Stylist: 'no vosso nome' sounds unnatural in an invocation, the current locution being 'em vosso nome'. Refused as the text: the glossary keeps the article before possessives (o vosso nome) and the line would then have 'em vosso … no vosso' for one Latin construction said twice. If Gustavo ever rules on the article rule for fixed locutions, this is the place it bites.

options.label: pelo vosso nome … pelo vosso poder
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 / pt-PT / Douay-Rheims for the first colon. Clearer; resolves the preposition, and would leave 53:7 'na vossa verdade' standing alone. The ambiguity reader heard 'no vosso nome' as 'by God's power or authority' first, 'by invoking the name' second — both are in the Latin.

decisions.why: salvum fácere is the Latin psalter's standing phrase for σῴζω (the LXX here has the plain imperative σῶσον), beside the rarer salváre. It is a formula — Salvum me fac, Deus (68:2), Salvum me fac, Dómine (11:2), Dómine, salvum fac regem (19:10) — so it needs one rendering.

options.label: salvai-me
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT, DM1962 and Douay-Rheims ('Save me'). The plainer of two faithful renderings; 'salvai' is safe under rule 3 (the past is 'salvei'). Cost: salvum fácere and salváre become one verb, as they are one verb in the Greek. The colon runs 2 syllables short of the Latin.

options.label: fazei-me salvo
options.note: Word for word, exactly the Latin's eleven syllables, and it keeps salvum fácere apart from salváre; but it is a calque nobody prays, and 'salvo' needs a feminine twin for a woman praying alone.

decisions.latin: … salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua júdica me.
decisions.why: In the Latin's order the two cola end 'salvai-me' / 'julgai-me': a full rhyme at mediant and final, which rule 5 counts a defect. The Latin's own echo there is only the pronoun (me fac / me).

options.label: e julgai-me no vosso poder
options.note: Draft. The first colon keeps the Latin's order, because it is the incipit and is read beside 'Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac'; the second takes the natural Portuguese order, which removes the rhyme and closes the verse on an oxytone. The stylist let the line stand in this order.

options.label: e no vosso poder julgai-me
options.note: The Latin's order and its parallelism in both cola, at the price of the rhyme salvai-me / julgai-me.

decisions.why: The ambiguity reader heard 'julgai-me' first as 'weigh my conduct and pass sentence on me', and only second as 'do justice to my cause'. The Latin 'júdica me' (κρῖνόν με) is open in exactly that way — Douay-Rheims leaves it 'judge me' — while Matos Soares 1932 and DM1962 settle it ('julga a minha causa', 'defende a minha causa').

options.label: julgai-me
options.note: Draft, kept. The Latin's two words and the Latin's openness; the man who asks to be saved 'in the name' also asks to be judged 'in the power', and the prayer is bolder for it. The same two words open 7:9b, 25:1, 34:24 and 42:1 (Júdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam — where 'causa' is a word of its own), so the bare verb must be kept free.

options.label: julgai a minha causa
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. What the hearer needs in order to take the second reading at once; adds a noun and closes the first reading (rule 2).

decisions.why: virtus here is δύναμις, power. It is one of the psalter's heavy words — 72 verses by a quick count, from 'Dóminus virtútum' to 'déxtera Dómini fecit virtútem' (117:16, next in the order of work) to Pharaoh's army (135:15) — and it stands beside fortitúdo (67:36 virtútem et fortitúdinem) and poténtia (64:7 in virtúte tua, accínctus poténtia), so the three want three words. It wants a word study; this is a proposal for the singular 'in virtúte tua' only.

options.label: poder
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and DM1962. Plain, and it makes no false echo with 'os fortes' two verses on. Cost: it takes the natural word of potéstas / potens, which the word study will have to weigh.

options.label: força
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'strength'. Good for the verses where virtus fails a man (21:16, 30:11, 37:11, 70:9); here it would chime with 'fortes' in 53:5, which the Latin does not, and it is the natural word of fortitúdo.

options.label: virtude
options.note: The cognate. In current Portuguese 'virtude' is a moral quality; the sense 'power' survives only in 'em virtude de'. It would need the footnote rule 5 forbids.

decisions.why: áuribus percípere (ἐνωτίζομαι, 'to take into the ears'; L&S cites the psalter for percípere áuribus 'hear, give ear') occurs eight times, and in four of them, as here, it is the second member after exáudi (38:13, 53:4, 83:9, 142:1); in 85:6 it stands before inténde. So it needs a verb that is not escutar (exaudíre), not ouvir (audíre), not atender (inténdere), and that stays apart from 'inclína aurem tuam' (ten verses: 16:6, 30:3, 85:1, 87:3, 101:3 …). It must work with an object (verba, oratiónem, lácrimas) and with none (83:9 áuribus pércipe, Deus Jacob; 48:2 áuribus percípite omnes), and at the vós imperative.

options.label: dai ouvidos a
options.note: Draft, and the proposal for all eight places (tried in each: 5:2 'Dai ouvidos, Senhor, às minhas palavras'; 38:13 'dai ouvidos às minhas lágrimas'; 83:9 'dai ouvidos, Deus de Jacó'; 48:2 'dai ouvidos, todos vós que habitais o orbe'). Keeps the ears, which are the Latin's image; is living Brazilian Portuguese; 'dai' is safe under rule 3 (the past is 'dei'); Douay-Rheims has the same idiom ('give ear'), and pt-PT uses it once (5:2). Cost: in everyday speech 'dar ouvidos a' leans toward 'give credence to'. The blind readers bear it out: the stylist named 53:4 the best line of the psalm ('especially whole and natural'), the Latinist passed it, and the ambiguity reader found nothing to mishear in it.

options.label: prestai ouvidos a
options.note: pt-PT at 85:6 and 142:1. The same image, a little more formal, without the shade of 'believing'; 'prestai' is safe (past 'prestei'). Less said in Brazil than 'prestar atenção', and one syllable longer.

options.label: percebei com os ouvidos
options.note: Word for word (DM1962, though from the Hebrew, reaches for the same verb: 'que teus ouvidos percebam'). 'percebei' is safe (past 'percebi'), but the phrase is a calque, four syllables over, and cannot stand without an object (83:9, 48:2).

options.label: atendei a
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT in this verse. Refused: it is the glossary's verb for inténdere, which stands beside áuribus pércipe in 85:6, and it drops the ears.

decisions.why: aliéni (ἀλλότριοι: those who are another's, strangers) and fortes (κραταιοί, the mighty) stand without article in the Greek, which has one to use; the Latin cannot show the difference. Portuguese must choose between a bare plural and the generic article.

options.label: estranhos … fortes
options.note: Draft 2, from the stylist, who found the first colon too long for one breath and heard the articles as small delays in it. Indefinite, as in the Greek and in Douay-Rheims ('strangers'). In draft 1 this was my second option, held back because a bare plural before its verb can sound like a headline; the stylist's ear did not hear that, and it is grammar, where the ear rules (rule 2). The colon is now 4 syllables under the Latin's 28, accepted.

options.label: os estranhos … os fortes
options.note: Draft 1, with Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. The article is how Portuguese names a class, and it brings the colon nearer the Latin's length; two more unstressed syllables in the longest colon of the psalm.

options.label: os estrangeiros … os fortes
options.note: Narrows aliéni to foreigners by nation. The Latin word is wider: anyone who is not one's own (L&S: 'not related or allied, not friendly, strange').

decisions.why: insúrgere in / advérsum recurs for the enemies (3:2, 17:40, 26:12, 85:14, 91:12 …), beside exsúrgere and súrgere, which are said of God (Exsúrge, Dómine).

options.label: se levantaram contra mim
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and DM1962. The plainer of two faithful words. Cost: insúrgere and exsúrgere will share 'levantar-se', told apart only by 'contra'.

options.label: se insurgiram contra mim
options.note: The cognate, current in Brazil, and it keeps the enemies' verb apart from God's 'Levantai-vos'. Slightly newspaper in register.

decisions.latin: quæsiérunt ánimam meam … suscéptor est ánimæ meæ
decisions.why: ánima mea → 'a minha alma' is the glossary's working rule. The ambiguity reader heard both lines in the spiritual sense first — 'they sought to reach or seize my spiritual soul', 'the support of my spiritual soul' — and 'they sought to take my life' only second. ánima (ψυχή) is both; Portuguese 'alma' has narrowed. Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and DM1962 all write 'vida' in both verses; Douay-Rheims keeps 'soul'. This is a cost of the glossary entry, shown here where it is sharpest: quǽrere ánimam is the idiom for seeking someone's death.

options.label: a minha alma
options.note: Glossary, applied. The Latin's word, twice in two verses as the Latin has it, and the idiom left as an idiom; the hearer who takes 'alma' spiritually still prays something true of the enemies the Office has in mind.

options.label: a minha vida
options.note: Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT, DM1962. What the idiom means, heard at once; but vita is another Latin word, and the glossary would then need a rule for when ánima is which.

decisions.why: conspéctus is 'sight, view' (ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν), and 'in conspéctu' is everywhere in the psalter. In this psalm the eye itself comes in 53:9 (óculus meus), so a rendering with 'olhos' here would make a link the Latin does not make.

options.label: diante da sua vista
options.note: Draft. 'vista' is conspéctus; the colon comes to the Latin's fifteen syllables. Cost: 'sua' is not reflexive by form as 'suum' is — the hearer resolves it by sense (no one sets God before God's own sight).

options.label: diante de si
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Native and unambiguously reflexive; conspéctus goes unheard and the colon falls 4–5 syllables short.

options.label: diante dos seus olhos
options.note: Douay-Rheims ('before their eyes') and DM1962. The most natural phrase; refused as the text because óculus is another word, and it is coming in 53:9.

decisions.why: Portuguese may mark a personal direct object with 'a', and with 'Deus' it traditionally does (amar a Deus). Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and DM1962 all write 'a Deus' in this verse. The stylist heard the preposition as an artificial solemnity that comes between verb and object.

options.label: não puseram Deus
options.note: Draft 2, from the stylist. Grammar, where the ear rules (rule 2); nothing of the Latin is lost, and the tier-2 literal already had it. Draft 1 kept 'a' so that 'Deus' would not be heard as the subject, but the plural verb already shuts that out.

options.label: não puseram a Deus
options.note: Draft 1, with Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and DM1962. The traditional regency with the divine name, one syllable nearer the Latin.

decisions.why: adjuváre belongs with adjutórium → auxílio (Ps 90) and adjútor, which is all over the psalter (117:7 Dóminus mihi adjútor, next in the order of work). A present indicative in the Latin (βοηθεῖ μοι).

options.label: me auxilia
options.note: Draft. The verb of the glossary's noun, so that ádjuvat / adjutórium / adjútor stay one family (auxiliar / auxílio). A little stiff beside 'me ajuda'.

options.label: me ajuda
options.note: The cognate and the plainest word there is. It would split the family (ajudar / auxílio) unless adjutórium moves to 'ajuda', which Ps 90 weighed and found thin.

options.label: vem em meu auxílio
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Keeps the glossary's noun and sounds like prayer already known; but it adds a verb of motion, and it is the phrase the opening versicle of the Hours will want for another Latin (in adjutórium meum inténde).

decisions.why: Open in the glossary since Ps 90:2 (ἀντιλήμπτωρ: one who takes up, upholds). Here it has a genitive — the upholder of my soul — which tries the Ps 90 word in a new construction. Must stay apart from protéctor → protetor.

options.label: amparo
options.note: Ps 90:2, applied. 'O amparo da minha alma' is natural Portuguese; the cost is the same as there: an agent noun becomes an abstract one.

options.label: defensor
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 at 90:2 (here he has 'protector'). An agent noun; adds the idea of fighting.

options.label: arrimo
options.note: DM1962 in this verse ('o arrimo da minha vida') — from the Hebrew, so borrowed for the word only: a prop, what one leans on, alive in Brazil in 'arrimo de família'. Close to suscípere; rarer than 'amparo'.

options.label: protetor
options.note: Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT and Douay-Rheims here. Refused: it is the glossary's word for protéctor.

decisions.why: An imperative in the Latin (the LXX has a future, ἀποστρέψει: the Latin is followed). a-vértere is 'to turn away, turn off', here with a dative of the ones the evils are turned to. Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT paraphrase ('Faze recair … sobre').

options.label: Desviai os males para
options.note: Draft. 'desviar' is a-vértere (turn off its course), 'para' the dative; it can serve 'avérte fáciem tuam' elsewhere. 'Desviai' is safe under rule 3 (past 'desviei'). Two syllables over the Latin.

options.label: Fazei recair os males sobre
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Says where the evils came from (they fall back), which is the Greek ἀπο-; more than the Latin verb says, and two verbs for one.

options.label: Voltai os males contra
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'Turn back the evils upon'. Plain and the right length; 'contra' is stronger than a dative.

decisions.why: véritas → 'verdade' is the glossary's working word (Ps 90:5), chosen against the Hebrew-family 'fidelidade'. Here it is tried where it is hardest: God is asked to destroy 'in his truth' (ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ σου). The ambiguity reader heard 'according to what God recognises as true' first and 'by God's faithfulness to his word' second; Matos Soares 1932 keeps 'na tua verdade' and explains it in a footnote ('segundo as promessas que fizeste de me proteger sempre'). The twin line, 142:11b, has 'in misericórdia tua dispérdes inimícos meos', and 142:1 has this psalm's two phrases together (áuribus pércipe obsecratiónem meam in veritáte tua). The preposition follows the decision 'in'.

options.label: na vossa verdade
options.note: Glossary, applied; Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT, Douay-Rheims ('in thy truth'). The Latin's word, as wide as the Latin's: God's truth is also his being true to his word, and the hearer can reach that from 'verdade' as the Latin hearer does from véritas. Kept before the verb, as in the Latin.

options.label: na vossa fidelidade
options.note: DM1962 ('conforme a tua fidelidade'), from the Hebrew. It is the ambiguity reader's second reading made the only one; the Latin did not write fidélitas or fides, and the glossary has refused this word since Ps 90:5 (rule 1).

decisions.why: dispérdere (ἐξολεθρεύω, 'destroy utterly') comes about fifteen times, often of God and once in the twin of this very line (142:11b in misericórdia tua dispérdes inimícos meos). It is not dispérgere, 'scatter', which the psalter also has (58:12 Dispérge illos in virtúte tua). The obvious verb, destruir, fails rule 3: 'destruí-os' is also 'I destroyed them'.

options.label: exterminai-os
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. As strong as the Greek, safe at every form under vós, paroxytone at the close. The Latin's own extermináre occurs once (79:14), of a boar in a vineyard.

options.label: fazei-os perecer
options.note: Keeps the perd- / perish sense of dis-pérdere; but it is a periphrasis, and períre is a verb of its own in the psalter (91:10 inimíci tui períbunt).

options.label: destruí-os
options.note: Douay-Rheims has 'cut them off'; this is the everyday verb. Refused: the vós imperative equals the first-person past (rule 3).

decisions.why: ἑκουσίως: of my own will, unforced — the word of the freewill offering. Matos Soares 1932 turns the adverb into an adjective of a noun he supplies ('um sacrifício voluntário').

options.label: De livre vontade
options.note: Draft. Keeps voluntas in 'vontade' and is how Portuguese says 'voluntarily'; 'livre' belongs to the idiom (Douay-Rheims: 'freely'). DM1962 says the same ('por livre vontade').

options.label: Voluntariamente
options.note: The cognate, word for word; six syllables of office Portuguese at the head of a verse of praise.

options.label: De bom grado
options.note: Shorter and warm; 'gladly' rather than 'of my own will', and the root is lost.

decisions.why: One verb in the Latin (θύσω σοι), with no noun. The stylist found 'sacrificarei a vós' understandable but translated, and asked for 'oferecer sacrifício'. The verb is rare in the psalter (4:6, 53:8, 105:38, 106:22, 115:7b), but in two of those places the Latin sets it beside its own noun — 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium justítiæ, 106:22 sacríficent sacrifícium laudis — and Ps 4:6 is already 'Sacrificai um sacrifício de justiça'.

options.label: sacrificarei a vós
options.note: Draft, kept. The Latin's verb, the same as in Ps 4:6, so that 'sacrificáre sacrifícium' can go on repeating where the Latin repeats (rule 6). The stressed 'a vós' after the verb because 'vos sacrificarei' can be heard as 'I will sacrifice you'. The stylist's hearing is granted: it sounds translated.

options.label: oferecerei sacrifício a vós
options.note: Stylist. More native in prayer, and the act stays concrete. Refused as the text under rule 2: it supplies a noun the Latin does not have here (Matos Soares 1932 does the same, 'Eu te oferecerei um sacrifício voluntário'), and with 'oferecer' as the verb 4:6 and 106:22 would lose their repetition. Three syllables over.

decisions.why: confitéri to God (ἐξομολογέομαι) is open in the glossary, with 'louvar' pencilled in; the family is in 74 verses (count.py, the noun conféssio included). Three facts from the Latin psalter bear on it. It stands in one verse with laudáre as its parallel (34:18 Confitébor tibi … laudábo te; 108:30 Confitébor Dómino … laudábo eum; 105:47 confiteámur … in laude tua), so 'louvar' for both would make one word of two. 'grátias ágere' never occurs in the psalms, so 'dar graças' is free. And confitéri to God always has a dative (tibi, Dómino, nómini tuo, memóriæ sanctitátis ejus), which 'dar graças a' keeps and 'louvar' cannot. Here the setting is a freewill sacrifice after a rescue; the same three words close 137:1b–2a (et confitébor nómini tuo). This is a proposal for the whole psalter, not a ruling: Ps 117, next in the order of work, opens and closes on the verb and will follow what is recorded here.

options.label: darei graças ao vosso nome
options.note: Draft and proposal. Keeps the dative, fits the thank-offering, leaves 'louvar' to laudáre, and works at the form that matters most: 'Dai graças ao Senhor, porque ele é bom' ('dai' is safe under rule 3: the past is 'dei'). Tried in the hard places: 117:21 'Eu vos darei graças, porque me escutastes'; 6:6 'quem vos dará graças?'; 29:5 'dai graças à memória da sua santidade'. Costs: the root of confession — acknowledging aloud — is heard only faintly in thanksgiving; and the noun conféssio will not always follow ('ação de graças' fits 41:5, 94:2, 99:3b, 146:7, but not 95:6, 103:1, 110:3, 148:14a, where it is God's own splendour).

options.label: louvarei o vosso nome
options.note: The glossary's pencilled word; Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT here, Douay-Rheims 'give praise'. Plain and beloved; collides with laudáre in the verses that have both, and turns the dative into a direct object.

options.label: celebrarei o vosso nome
options.note: A third verb that is neither laudáre's nor thanksgiving's; 'Celebrai o Senhor' is safe under rule 3 (past 'celebrei'). Wider and vaguer than the Latin (to celebrate is not to acknowledge), no dative, and it would serve conféssio no better.

options.label: confessarei ao vosso nome
options.note: The cognate, with the dative (tier 2 has it). In Portuguese 'confessar' to God is first of all confessing sins, which the glossary keeps for 31:5; 'Confessai ao Senhor' at the head of Pss 105, 106, 117, 135 would be misheard.

decisions.latin: et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est
decisions.why: The ambiguity reader heard 'porque é bom' first of all as 'because the Lord is good' — the one reading the Latin's neuter shuts out (see 'bonum'). In draft 1 the vocative 'Senhor' stood, as in the Latin, right before 'porque é bom', and the ear took it for the subject, helped by the refrain 'Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus'. Latin keeps the readings apart by gender; Portuguese can only do it by order.

options.label: e darei graças, Senhor, ao vosso nome: porque é bom
options.note: Draft 2. The vocative moves up one place, so that 'o vosso nome' is what stands before 'porque é bom'. Every word of the Latin is there, the inner colon stays, the count is the same, and both of the Latin's readings stay open (the name is good; it is good to do so). Order is what rule 2 lets the ear have. Cost: the Portuguese no longer runs word for word under 'nómini tuo, Dómine'.

options.label: e darei graças ao vosso nome, Senhor: porque é bom
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's order (so Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT). Strictly the grammar already excludes the Lord as subject — he is addressed as 'vós', and 'é' is third person — but the blind reader's ear did not stop at that.

decisions.why: bonum is neuter: either the name is good (nomen is neuter; so 98:3 Confiteántur nómini tuo magno: quóniam terríbile et sanctum est) or it is good to do so (91:2 Bonum est confitéri Dómino). The nearest parallel favours the name without settling it: 51:11 exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum. It is not 'the Lord is good', which would be bonus, as in the refrain (105:1, 117:1 Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus). Portuguese has no neuter, so every rendering shifts the ambiguity a little. The ambiguity reader heard exactly the excluded reading first ('porque o Senhor é bom'), then the name, then the act; the answer in draft 2 is one of order (see 'v8b'), not of words.

options.label: porque é bom
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Both of the Latin's readings stay possible (o nome é bom; é bom fazê-lo). Cost: the hearer may also take 'Senhor' as the subject, which the Latin's gender rules out — the blind reader did; draft 2 moves the vocative away from it rather than change these words.

options.label: porque é coisa boa
options.note: Makes the neuter audible and shuts out 'the Lord is good'; but it leans to the second reading and adds a noun.

options.label: porque ele é bom
options.note: The first reading only (the name), and in the mouth it becomes the refrain 'porque ele é bom' of Confitémini Dómino, where the Latin has the masculine bonus. Refused: it resolves.

decisions.why: erípere is open in the glossary from Ps 90:15 (arrancar), kept apart from liberáre → livrar. Here it has its 'from' (ex omni tribulatióne), which is where 'arrancar' is at its most natural. LXX ἐρρύσω.

options.label: arrancastes
options.note: Ps 90:15, applied: 'de toda tribulação me arrancastes' — snatched out of, the image of e-rípere.

options.label: libertastes
options.note: Smoother; the cognate of the other verb, liberáre.

options.label: livrastes
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ('tens-me livrado'), pt-PT, DM1962, Douay-Rheims 'delivered'. Native; merges erípere with liberáre.

decisions.latin: et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus
decisions.why: despícere is literally 'to look down upon' and by figure 'to despise' (L&S); with 'super' + accusative and the eye as subject the Latin has the literal picture (LXX ἐπεῖδεν ἐν, 'looked upon'; Douay-Rheims 'my eye hath looked down upon my enemies'). Portuguese happens to have the same double sense in one idiom, 'olhar de cima', and the ambiguity reader heard all three of the Latin's senses in it (from a higher place; in superiority or victory — the likeliest; with contempt). The trouble is the ear: 'o meu olho olhou' repeats a root the Latin does not repeat (despéxit / óculus). The stylist named this the worst line of draft 1 on two counts — the subject comes late, after two displaced complements, and 'olhou … olho' echo — and his own alternative mends the first by putting the two words side by side. The verb is said of enemies again in 91:12 (Et despéxit óculus meus inimícos meos — the eye again, with a plain accusative), 111:7b and 117:7 (et ego despíciam inimícos meos — next in the order of work, no eye: 'olharei de cima os meus inimigos' runs clean).

options.label: e o meu olho olhou de cima para os meus inimigos

forms.despexit: e o meu olho olhou de cima para os meus inimigos

options.note: Draft 2, the stylist's line. Natural order — order is what rule 2 gives to the ear — with the idiom whole, the eye singular, and 'para' answering 'super' (91:12, which has the bare accusative, would be 'olhou de cima os meus inimigos'). Cost, not hidden: 'olho olhou' now stand together. Draft 1 kept them apart and the stylist heard the echo all the same, so the Latin's order bought nothing for the ear; the echo belongs to the pair olho / olhar and only another verb removes it (next option but one).

options.label: e sobre os meus inimigos olhou de cima o meu olho

forms.despexit: e sobre os meus inimigos olhou de cima o meu olho

options.note: Draft 1. The Latin's own order (super inimícos meos / despéxit / óculus meus), with 'super' → 'sobre' and three words between 'olhou' and 'olho'. The stylist's worst line: subject late, 'olhar sobre' not everyday regency, and the echo heard anyway.

options.label: e o meu olho viu de cima os meus inimigos

forms.despexit: e o meu olho viu de cima os meus inimigos

options.note: Natural order and no echo at all (the Greek verb is in fact 'saw upon'); but 'ver de cima' has only the literal sense, so the contempt in despícere is lost, and the verb would then differ from 117:7.

options.label: e o meu olho olhou com desprezo para os meus inimigos

forms.despexit: e o meu olho olhou com desprezo para os meus inimigos

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (he has 'os meus olhos olharam'). Explains the image instead of giving it, and has the echo too.

choices.53:3: The psalm begins at 53:3 (53:1–2 are the title, which the Office does not say). júdica me → 'julgai-me', bare, as in the Latin; Matos Soares 1932 and DM1962 expand it ('julga a minha causa', 'defende a minha causa') — see the decision 'judica', added after the ambiguity reader. 'julgai' is safe under rule 3 (past 'julguei'). 'no vosso nome' kept against the stylist's 'em vosso nome' (decision 'in'). First colon 3 syllables short of the Latin by the checker, with 'salvai-me'; accepted.
choices.53:4: exáudi → 'escutai' (glossary, working): the formula 'Senhor, escutai a minha oração' with the Latin's vocative, 'Deus'. verba oris mei → 'as palavras da minha boca': the mouth stays (DM1962 'lábios' is the Hebrew-family habit). The second colon is the glossary proposal for áuribus percípere — see the decision.
choices.53:5: No flex in the Latin, so none here: the first colon is the longest of the psalm (28 syllables in Latin by the checker) and is said on the tenor. Draft 2 takes two of the stylist's three proposals for this verse, both matters of grammar: the bare plurals 'estranhos … fortes' (decision 'alieni') and 'puseram Deus' without 'a' (decision 'deum'). His other two changes in the same line are refused: 'Pois' for 'Porque', because Quóniam is 'Porque' three times in the psalm (53:5, 53:8, 53:9) as in the Latin, and 'Pois' is kept for enim in 53:6; and 'minha alma' without the article, against the glossary (a minha alma). quæsiérunt ánimam meam → 'buscaram a minha alma': ánima mea → a minha alma (glossary), not 'vida' (Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT, DM1962) — see the decision 'animam'; quǽrere → buscar as in Ps 4:3. proposuérunt → 'puseram … diante': the pro- is carried by 'diante'; 'propuseram' would mean 'proposed'. The ambiguity reader asked whether 'estranhos' are unknown people or odd ones, whether 'fortes' are strong in body or in power, and whether both groups or only the second forgot God: each time the Latin is open in the same way (aliéni, fortes, one plural verb), and the likelier hearing was the right one; nothing changed.
choices.53:6: Ecce enim → 'Pois eis que' (ἰδοὺ γάρ); Matos Soares 1932 has 'Mas eis que', which is not enim. ádjuvat is a present: 'me auxilia'. 'est' kept as 'é'. ánimæ meæ → 'da minha alma'.
choices.53:7: The Latin has an imperative (Avérte) where the LXX has a future; the Latin is followed. véritas → 'verdade' (glossary, Ps 90:5), not the Hebrew-family 'fidelidade' (DM1962) — see the decision 'veritate'; 'in veritáte tua' → 'na vossa verdade', the same 'in' as in 53:3, and kept before the verb as in the Latin: the verse closes on the imperative. mala → 'os males', plural and concrete; the ambiguity reader heard 'sufferings, dangers' first and 'wicked deeds' second, which is the range of mala. He also asked whether 'os' in 'exterminai-os' are the enemies or the evils: in the Latin illos is masculine and mala neuter, so it is the enemies, and that is what he heard first.
choices.53:8: sacrificábo tibi → 'sacrificarei a vós': sacrificáre → sacrificar as in Ps 4:6; the stylist's 'oferecerei sacrifício' is an option (decision 'sacrificabo'). The stressed 'a vós' after the verb because 'vos sacrificarei' can be heard as 'I will sacrifice you' (pt-PT's 'Sacrificar-me-ei … a Vós' is a slip of another kind). Draft 2 moves the vocative: 'e darei graças, Senhor, ao vosso nome: porque é bom' (decision 'v8b'), so that the name and not 'Senhor' stands before 'porque é bom'. The verse ends on a colon, as in the Latin, because 53:9 depends on it; 'porque … : / Porque …' repeats as 'quóniam … : / Quóniam …' does (Matos Soares 1932 varies it: 'porque … Porquanto'). Second colon 2 syllables short of the Latin by the checker: nothing is left out. Douay-Rheims reads 'O God' where this Latin has Dómine; the Latin is followed. confitébor → 'darei graças' is the glossary proposal of this psalm (decision 'confitebor').
choices.53:9: eripuísti is a perfect: 'me arrancastes' (Matos Soares' 'tens-me livrado' is iterative in Brazil). 'de toda tribulação' without the article, which in Brazil is 'every' (ex omni), where 'toda a tribulação' would be 'the whole of the'. tribulátio → tribulação (glossary). First colon 4 short of the Latin, accepted; naming the subject ('vós me arrancastes') would mend the count and is unnecessary. óculus meus → 'o meu olho', singular as in the Latin (Matos Soares 1932 and DM1962 make it plural). Second colon: draft 2 takes the stylist's natural order, with 'olho olhou' side by side — see the decision 'despexit', where draft 1's line is the second option.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm53.txt, seven prayed verses, 53:3–53:9, each with one '*' and no other mark. The Hetzenauer 1914 print read was skipped overnight and is owed.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps053.md (Douay-Rheims there is the right psalm this time; the pt-PT block is numbered 53:1–7 for 53:3–9, and words/percipere.concordance.md pairs the pt-PT lines wrongly for the same reason). Lewis & Short consulted for percípio, despício, dispérdo, aliénus (letters A, P, V fetched into consult/). ps053/count.py is a scratch counter over the DO Latin psalter, used for the glossary proposals (dispérdere, despícere, virtus, confitéri beside laudáre, grátias, inclína aurem). Latin against the LXX: imperative Avérte (53:7) where the Greek has a future — the Latin followed. Rule 3 checked at every imperative: salvai, julgai, escutai, dai, desviai, exterminai all differ from their first-person past; destruir was refused for dispérde on that ground.

Draft 1: hard pass (ids and marks). Soft: 53:3 first colon −3 (accepted: 'salvai-me' is the plain word; both longer options are in the decisions 'deus' and 'salvum'); 53:7 first colon +3 (accepted: 'para os' runs together in the mouth; the shorter 'Voltai os males contra' is an option); 53:9 first colon −4 (accepted: nothing is left out; 'vós me arrancastes' would add a syllable only). No rhyme or cadence flags.
Draft 1 (prayed.v1.vos.json). Clean: no verse remarked; content, verb forms, images and every mark confirmed.

Draft 1. Five remarks in four verses; best line 53:4 (the 'dai ouvidos' line), worst 53:9. Three taken, all matters of grammar or order (53:5 bare plurals, 53:5 'Deus' without 'a', 53:9 natural order); two refused as the text and kept as options (53:3 'em vosso nome', 53:8 'oferecerei sacrifício'). Inside the 53:5 proposal, 'Pois' for 'Porque' and 'minha alma' without the article were not taken.

outcomes.remark: 'no vosso nome' unnatural in an invocation → 'em vosso nome'
outcomes.reason: The glossary keeps the article before possessives, and the line would say one Latin construction two ways ('em vosso … no vosso').

outcomes.remark: first colon too long for one breath; the articles delay it → 'Pois estranhos … e fortes buscaram minha alma'
outcomes.reason: Taken for the articles only (grammar, rule 2). 'Pois' refused: Quóniam is 'Porque' three times in the psalm and 'Pois' is enim in 53:6. 'minha alma' without the article refused: glossary.

outcomes.remark: 'a Deus' — the preposition is an artificial solemnity → 'não puseram Deus'
'sacrificarei a vós' sounds translated → 'oferecerei sacrifício a vós'
outcomes.reason: Rule 2: it supplies a noun the Latin does not have here, and with 'oferecer' as the verb 4:6 and 106:22 (sacrificáre sacrifícium) would lose their repetition; Ps 4:6 is already 'Sacrificai um sacrifício'.

outcomes.remark: subject arrives late after two displaced complements; 'olhou … olho' echo → 'e o meu olho olhou de cima para os meus inimigos'

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. Twelve items, no unknown words. One real fault: 53:8 'porque é bom' was heard first as 'the Lord is good', which the Latin's neuter excludes — acted on by moving the vocative (decision 'v8b'). Four show the cost of the Latin's or the glossary's words and live on as options in decisions (53:3 julgai-me; 53:5 and 53:6 'alma' heard as the spiritual soul before 'life'; 53:7 'verdade'). The other seven are the Latin's own openness, in most of them heard the right way first; nothing changed. 'dai ouvidos' raised no remark.

outcomes.remark: 'no vosso nome': by God's power or authority / by invoking the name
outcomes.reason: Both readings are in the Latin 'in nómine tuo' (ἐν); recorded in the decision 'in', text unchanged.

outcomes.remark: 'julgai-me' heard first as 'pass sentence on me', second as 'do justice to my cause'
outcomes.reason: The Latin 'júdica me' is open in exactly this way; 'julgai a minha causa' (MS1932) is offered as the option.

outcomes.remark: 'os estranhos': unknown / outsiders, or people of odd behaviour
outcomes.reason: The right sense was the one heard first; aliéni → estranhos kept (the narrower 'estrangeiros' is in the decision 'alieni').

outcomes.remark: 'os fortes': strong in body, or powerful
outcomes.reason: fortes (κραταιοί) is open in the same way; 'poderosos' would settle it and would take the word of potens.

outcomes.remark: 'buscaram a minha alma' heard first as seizing my spiritual soul, second as taking my life
outcomes.reason: Glossary ánima mea → a minha alma kept; 'a minha vida' (MS1932, pt-PT, DM1962) offered.

outcomes.remark: 'não puseram a Deus diante da sua vista': both groups, or only the strong
outcomes.reason: The Latin has the same single plural verb after two subjects; heard of both first, which is the natural reading.

outcomes.remark: 'o amparo da minha alma': of my spiritual soul, or of my life, of me whole
outcomes.reason: Same glossary cost as in 53:5; the two verses move together in one decision.

outcomes.remark: 'os males': sufferings and dangers, or wicked deeds
outcomes.reason: mala has the same range; the first hearing is the likelier sense.

outcomes.remark: 'na vossa verdade': according to what God holds true, or by God's faithfulness to his word
outcomes.reason: véritas → verdade is the glossary's word and as wide as the Latin's; 'fidelidade' (DM1962, from the Hebrew) is offered and argued against.
illos is masculine and mala neuter, so the enemies — which is what was heard first; no change needed.

outcomes.remark: 'porque é bom' heard first as 'the Lord is good', then the name, then the act of thanking
outcomes.reason: The first hearing is the one reading bonum (neuter) excludes. The words are kept and the vocative moved so that 'o vosso nome' stands before 'porque é bom'.

outcomes.remark: 'olhou de cima': from a higher place / in superiority or victory / with contempt
outcomes.reason: All three are despícere super; the idiom carries the Latin's range, and that is why it was chosen.

Found done by the first agent: prayed.v1.json / prayed.v1.vos.json saved; the decisions 'alieni' (bare plurals taken), 'in' (stylist option), 'judica' and 'animam' (from the ambiguity reader); 'a Deus' → 'Deus' in the verse. Found half-done: 53:8 pointed at two slots that did not exist (sacrificabo, v8b), 'bonum' was orphaned, choices and audit still described draft 1, and version/status had been bumped ahead of the work. Done by the second agent: decisions 'deum', 'veritate', 'sacrificabo', 'v8b' (vocative moved in 53:8), 'confitebor' split into two slots with a fourth option, 'despexit' reordered on the stylist's line (and its 'why' corrected: 91:12 does have the eye); choices, audit, glossary, PROGRESS. Wording changed against draft 1 in 53:5 (estranhos … fortes; puseram Deus), 53:8 (darei graças, Senhor, ao vosso nome) and 53:9 (e o meu olho olhou de cima para os meus inimigos). Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the v1 critics read). Owed: the Hetzenauer 1914 print read of the Latin, skipped overnight. ps053/count.py is kept: the verse counts quoted in the decisions come from it.

Draft 2: hard pass (ids and marks). Soft: 53:3 first colon −3, 53:7 first colon +3, 53:9 first colon −4, all as in draft 1 and accepted for the same reasons. New: 53:5 first colon −4 (24 against the Latin's 28) — the price of the stylist's bare plurals, accepted: the colon is the longest of the psalm, has no flex, and he asked for it to be shortened for the breath; the articles are one click away in the decision 'alieni'. 53:8 second colon still 17 against 19 after the vocative moved. No rhyme or cadence flags.

Draft 2 (prayed.vos.json), run because 53:5, 53:8 and 53:9 changed. Clean again: no verse remarked — sense, persons, tenses, moods and every mark confirmed, the moved vocative of 53:8 and the new order of 53:9 included. The gate is clean.
